update_log: Exhaustive compilation of major Indian lakes (categorized by extremes/types) and high-frequency waterfalls (matched with their rivers) for Geography Static GK.

major_lakes_of_india.key_fact: One of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, formed as a result of tectonic activity. The Jhelum river feeds it.
India's largest coastal lagoon and the largest wintering ground for migratory birds on the Indian sub-continent.
The longest lake in India. Famous for hosting the annual Nehru Trophy Boat Race (Vallam Kali).
The largest freshwater lake in North-East India. Famous for the circular floating islands called 'Phumdis' and hosts the Keibul Lamjao (the world's only floating national park).
India's largest inland salt lake, representing a large endorheic basin.
A highly unique crater lake formed by a meteorite impact during the Pleistocene Epoch.
The highest lake in India, situated at an altitude of over 5,300 meters.
The second-largest brackish water lagoon in India. The barrier island of Sriharikota (Satish Dhawan Space Centre) separates it from the Bay of Bengal.
Located between the deltas of the Krishna and Godavari rivers.
India's largest artificial (man-made) lake, created by the Rihand Dam.
An endorheic lake in the Himalayas situated at about 4,350 meters. It freezes completely in winter despite being saline water. Lies on the Sino-Indian border.

major_waterfalls_of_india.key_fact: The highest waterfall in India (approx 455 meters), featuring a tiered cascade.
One of the highest plunge waterfalls in India. Famous for its four distinct cascades: Raja, Rani, Rover, and Rocket.
The tallest plunge waterfall in India (340 meters), located near Cherrapunji, one of the wettest places on Earth.
Literally translates to 'Sea of Milk'. Located on the Goa-Karnataka border, famously intersecting with the Madgaon-Belagavi rail route.
Widely known as the 'Niagara of India' because it is the widest waterfall in India during the monsoon season.
The site of Asia's first hydro-electric power station, set up in 1902.
Located at Bhedaghat in Jabalpur, famous for cascading through spectacular marble rocks.
A majestic two-tiered waterfall located deep within the Simlipal National Park.
One of the most famous waterfalls in the Chota Nagpur Plateau region, near Ranchi.
The largest waterfall in Kerala, often nicknamed the 'Niagara of South India'.
